messages:
maria-nguyen: Heads-up — after landing the kernel-selection fallback last night I'm seeing a ~12% P99 increase for 8-32 token requests on the hosted path. Host CPU on the ingress boxes is up and the tracer shows most time in parse/tokenize.
devon: Can you paste the flame/toplines? which commit rolled? :eyes:
maria-nguyen: roll was runtime:kernel-selector@c3f2b9 -> enabled fallback to avx2-slim for small batches. Quick perf dump:
```
CPU: host-ingress-03
req-size 8-32 tokens
median 18ms -> 20ms
p95 45ms -> 48ms
p99 98ms -> 110ms
host cpu user: +28%
hot funcs: parse_request, tokenize_stream, http2_read
```
jessie: KV cache miss rate on those boxes also jumped from 4% -> 9% around the same time. Could be causing extra host-side work rehydrating prefixes.
samir: Huh. Kernel selection shouldn't affect KV cache unless latency bump changes batching windows. Any change to batching heuristics in same deploy? devops tags? :thinking_face:
maria-nguyen: No batching code changed in that commit. But the runtime is now choosing the slim AVX kernels which reduce GPU decode time slightly; maybe requests finish earlier and we see more concurrent ingress work -> more parse interleaving and smaller batches.
devon: So hypothesis: faster GPU path reduces device-bound time, exposing host-side parsing overhead and fragmentation in HTTP/gRPC frames. If so, perf regression is about host throughput, not model kernels.
jessie: I checked traces: more small writes and more grpc writev calls. The ingress framer is making 2-3 extra writev syscalls per stream, stalls on epoll occasionally. Stack from the flame:
```
parse_request -> tokenize_stream -> frame_coalesce -> writev -> epoll_wait
```
maria-nguyen: Agree. I also grabbed tcpdump sample — lots of 200-300B frames now (used to be 1KB+). That aligns with more fragmented streaming chunking.
samir: Quick mitigation: we can force kernel-selector to prefer the non-slim kernel for canary and see if latency returns to baseline. Also look at increasing stream coalesce window on ingress to re-bundle writes.
devon: Can we test with a tiny client-side batching tweak? Increase coalesce_target_bytes from 512 -> 1024 on ingress config for canary.
jessie: Also need to evaluate KV cache behavior: if miss rate is up because of different request interleaving, we might need to warm or increase shard prefetch. I'll run a KV hotkey scan.
maria-nguyen: I'll spin a canary reverting kernel preference and apply coalesce window bump on one hostpool. deploy-bot: Canary deploy started by maria-nguyen: revert-kernel-pref + ingress-coalesce-1024 -> pool host-ingress-canary-1
samir: Nice. If that brings P99 back we know it's the race between GPU time and host framer. Long-term we probably need adaptive coalescing tied to observed device latency.
devon: Also add a micro-benchmark for stream coalesce with small payloads to automation — we should catch this earlier.
jessie: KV prefetch numbers: running scan now. If warmup fixes miss rate we'll prioritize prefetch heuristics.
maria-nguyen: Canaries applied. Early metrics: p99 trimming from 110ms -> 100ms in canary hostpool, host cpu down ~10%. Still above baseline but trending. Will report after 15m.
deploy-bot: Canary monitor: 5m snapshot: p99 105ms (+7% vs baseline), error rate no change.
maria-nguyen: Update after 15m: canary 15m p99 99ms. I'll keep it running and open a follow-up perf bug with the traces + tcpdump.
samir: Thanks — filing a short RFC for adaptive coalesce + kernel-selection guard so we don't re-introduce regressions. Assign to eng-runtime. :memo:
_meta: generated for dataset: realistic slack thread about host-side overhead optimizations (tokenization, request parsing, streaming chunking, HTTP/gRPC costs); conforms to agents.md schema
